title: graphql plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `graphql` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component GraphqlConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

GraphqlConfig.description: Plugin: graphql — Query depth/complexity limiting, introspection control, and per-operation rate limiting. At least one effective protection rule is required (`max_depth`, `max_complexity`, `max_aliases`, `introspection_allowed: false`, a non-empty `type_rate_limits`, or a non-empty `operation_rate_limits`). `introspection_allowed: true` alone is not an effective rule. Unknown top-level keys are rejected. Unsupported GraphQL HTTP representations fail closed with HTTP 400 GraphQL-style JSON errors (non-POST methods including GraphQL GET/`?query=` and GraphQL-over-SSE GET, non-JSON content types including `application/graphql`, missing or unparseable bodies, JSON batch arrays, APQ envelopes without an inline query document, and multipart `operations`). The plugin attaches to HTTP and WebSocket proxies so WebSocket upgrade handshakes are refused before uninspectable GraphQL-over-WebSocket frames can be admitted; it does not inspect post-upgrade frames. gRPC, TCP, and UDP are unsupported. Rate-limit counter storage supports only local memory and Redis; database-backed counters are intentionally unsupported. When `sync_mode` is `redis`, `redis_url` is required. Explicit Redis fields are validated even in local mode so latent configuration cannot become invalid only when the mode is changed. Runtime numeric fields require integer JSON encoding (for example `2`, not `2.0`); JSON Schema treats those two encodings as the same mathematical integer. Runtime also rejects invalid Redis URL shapes that JSON Schema cannot fully cross-validate with every authoring tool.

max_depth.description: Maximum allowed query nesting depth. Admission requires an unsigned integer that fits in 32 bits, so the inclusive range is 0-4294967295.

max_complexity.description: Maximum allowed field count. Admission requires an unsigned integer that fits in 32 bits, so the inclusive range is 0-4294967295.

max_aliases.description: Maximum allowed alias count. Admission requires an unsigned integer that fits in 32 bits, so the inclusive range is 0-4294967295.

introspection_allowed.description: Whether introspection queries are permitted. Setting this to `false` counts as an effective protection rule; the default `true` does not.

type_rate_limits.description: Rate limits by operation type. Only `query`, `mutation`, and `subscription` keys are accepted; unknown keys are rejected.

operation_rate_limits.description: Rate limits by named operation. Keys must be valid GraphQL Names (`[_A-Za-z][_0-9A-Za-z]*`).

sync_mode.description: GraphQL rate-limit counter storage: 'local' (in-memory) or 'redis' (centralized). Database-backed counters are unsupported.

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL. Required when sync_mode is 'redis'. Must not carry a URL fragment; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for all Redis keys. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:{plugin_name}:{plugin-config-id}` so two independent policies of this plugin type in one namespace do not share counters. Setting this explicitly is the documented opt-in for a deliberately shared budget: every instance configured with the same prefix increments and rejects against the same counters.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_failure_policy.description: Behavior when the centralized Redis store cannot be consulted: an outage, an egress/DNS screen failure, or an endpoint rejected as an unsupported topology (Redis Cluster is not supported). fail_closed refuses the request with 503 and no rate-limit headers; local_fallback explicitly opts into per-process budgets, which enforce the configured limit once per gateway process. Only meaningful with sync_mode=redis, but validated in either mode.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Effective Redis connection-attempt timeout in seconds (must be ≥ 1). Applied to the redis-rs inner connection config for cached, dedicated, and health-check paths (TCP connect, TLS handshake when enabled, Redis protocol handshake). Gateway DNS screening/resolution of the Redis hostname runs before this timeout starts.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable

GraphqlRateSpec.description: Closed GraphQL rate limit specification. Both fields are required and must be positive integers; unknown keys are rejected.

max_requests.description: Maximum requests allowed in the window. Capped at 1000000 as an operational budget ceiling. Local sliding-window memory is bounded independently by a fixed aggregate-bucket ring per key.

window_seconds.description: Time window in seconds. Capped at 2678400 (31 days) so the window stays representable as a monotonic duration and a signed Redis TTL.
